animations.title: AD forest / domain tree
animations.description: Animated SVG of the lab.local domain: the domain root node expands into the five OUs (Workstations, Servers, Users, Groups, ServiceAccounts), each OU expanding to show its member objects (users, computers, groups) with distinct icons. Clicking any object shows its key attributes (DN, SID, memberOf). A replication animation draws pulsing arrows between the DC node and a (future) second DC, with a toggle for 'what replicates' (schema, configuration, domain partitions). A time-slider shows the promotion sequence: standalone server -> AD DS installed -> forest created -> DNS integrated.

animations.title: Zero Trust request flow
animations.description: Step-through SVG animation of a single access request under Zero Trust: (1) user/device on LAN requests the file share, (2) request hits the policy engine (identity check: who + device health + MFA), (3) explicit allow/deny decision rendered as a gate, (4) encrypted session to the resource, (5) continuous verification ticking in the background. Each step highlights with a caption explaining the principle ('never trust, always verify', 'least privilege', 'assume breach'). A toggle switches between 'flat network' (request walks straight through, red flags) and 'segmented' (request passes the gate, green) to show why the IL-27 lab segments LAN/DMZ.

animations.title: DHCP DORA sequence
animations.description: Animated sequence diagram of DHCP DORA: client broadcasts DISCOVER (packet expands to the broadcast domain), server responds OFFER (unicast, with offered IP highlighted), client broadcasts REQUEST, server answers ACK. Each packet is drawn with its real fields (op, xid, yiaddr, options 51/54/3/6) and the learner can hover any field for a plain-English explanation. A 'lease timeline' bar below shows T1/T2 renewal and expiry; pressing 'renew' replays REQUEST/ACK. A fault-injection toggle ('rogue server') shows a second OFFER racing the legitimate one, teaching why DHCP snooping exists.

animations.title: DNS resolution chain
animations.description: Full recursive-resolution walkthrough as an animated chain: stub resolver -> pfSense forwarder -> (root hints -> TLD -> authoritative) for an internet name, contrasted with the short path for lab.local (forwarder -> domain override -> LAB-DC01). Each hop lights up in order with the query/response packet contents shown; caching is visualized as a fading memory bar at each resolver ('TTL countdown'). The learner can type any name and watch the chain build; a toggle shows what breaks when the DC's DNS stops (lab.local goes dark while internet still resolves) — the exact IL27-BRANCH-02 incident, visualized.

animations.title: GPO processing order
animations.description: LSDOU processing order animated: Local -> Site -> Domain -> OU, with each layer's policies stacking onto a sample setting (e.g. screen-saver timeout) and later layers visibly overriding earlier ones. Toggles for 'Block Inheritance' (red X cuts the chain at that OU) and 'Enforced' (policy punches through the block, highlighted). A conflict demo sets the same setting at Domain and OU levels with different values and shows the winner plus WHY. Links to the learner's own lab: they can input their three IL27-TL-05 GPOs and watch them apply to a test computer object moving between OUs.

animations.title: Backup rotation scheme
animations.description: Interactive Grandfather-Father-Son rotation visualizer on a calendar canvas: daily incrementals (sons), weekly fulls (fathers), monthly fulls (grandfathers), with retention bars showing how far back each tier reaches. The learner drags the 'today' marker and the diagram highlights exactly which backup sets would restore any given date, computing the RPO. A 'disk cost' meter totals the storage consumed by the scheme vs a naive daily-full scheme. A disaster button ('file server dies on the 17th') walks the restore: pick the recovery point, list the sets needed (last full + incrementals since), and flag the data-loss window.

animations.title: Incident response lifecycle
animations.description: The six-phase IR lifecycle (Preparation -> Detection & Analysis -> Containment -> Eradication -> Recovery -> Lessons Learned) as a circular animated diagram. Clicking a phase expands it with the IL-27 lab's concrete actions (e.g. Containment: 'disable NIC at hypervisor'; Lessons Learned: 'write the report, add the AppLocker rule'). An animated scenario dot travels the circle using the ransomware drill timeline (2:14 PM detection -> 5 PM recovery), pausing at each phase with the actual action taken. Parse IIS log: top 5 requested URLs by hits.
log-parsing.answer: Get-Content u_ex*.log | Where { $_ -notlike '#*' } | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split ' ')[4] } | Group-Object | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select -First 5 Name, Count
solutionSteps: Split on spaces; field 4 (0-indexed) is cs-uri-stem

masteryModel.recheckPolicy: Proficient topics re-check with 3 spaced questions at 24h and 7d; a miss drops one level and queues remedial exercises. Mastery requires writing (not just recognizing) 5 generated solutions judged by the solution-steps rubric.
masteryModel.promotionRule: 8 consecutive correct mixed answers (2+ from generators) promotes a topic; scripting-constructs additionally requires one full written solution per promotion.
masteryModel.infinitePractice: Generators emit unbounded parameterized variants; the engine tracks per-template accuracy and biases toward weak templates (70/30 weak/strong mix), never repeating an exact question in a session.
masteryModel.masteryGating: Topics unlock in dependency order: cmdlets -> pipeline -> log-parsing -> scripting-constructs; ad-management requires cmdlets+pipeline at developing; services and network-diag require pipeline at developing. Locked topics show prerequisites, not questions.

masteryMap.spec: Per-learner JSON: {topicId: {level, correctStreak, attempts, weakTemplates[], writtenSolutions, lastRecheck, locked}}. Rendered as a 7-node dependency graph; nodes fill as levels rise, locked nodes greyed with prerequisite labels. The engine selects next question from the weakest unlocked topic.
